representative: Virus-level profile. Sequence length is from the Wuhan-Hu-1 reference isolate; particle measurements are from cryo-electron tomography of cultured, chemically fixed virions (Ke et al. 2020).
summary: An enveloped, positive-sense RNA virus with one of the largest RNA genomes known. Its genome can be translated directly on arrival, and it is packed by nucleocapsid protein into a loosely wound helical nucleocapsid rather than an icosahedral shell.

taxonomy.note: SARS-CoV-2 is an additional isolate of the species Betacoronavirus pandemicum (formerly Severe acute respiratory syndrome-related coronavirus); it is not the species exemplar. The suborder Cornidovirineae is omitted from the rank list.

lengthKb.note: Betacoronavirus genomes span 27–32 kb (ViralZone); coronaviruses overall ~22–36 kb (ICTV 2023).

capsid.value: No icosahedral capsid. The genome is bound by nucleocapsid protein in short helical units that are arranged loosely inside the envelope.

dimensions.label: Virion diameter (outside of membrane, excluding spikes)
dimensions.note: Mean ± SD of fixed virions; the bar spans one SD either side, not the full observed range.

dimensions.label: Coronaviridae family range
dimensions.note: Family-level range across coronaviruses; shown for context only.

site.value: Cytoplasm, on modified membranes and double-membrane vesicles

mRNARoute.value: The positive-sense genome is translated directly into replicase polyproteins. Negative-sense copies then serve as templates for new genomes and for a nested set of subgenomic mRNAs that share a 5′ leader.

steps.title: Attachment and entry
steps.text: The spike (S) protein binds host receptors and the particle enters by endocytosis.

steps.title: Genome release
steps.text: Viral and endosomal membranes fuse, releasing the genome into the cytoplasm.

steps.title: Replicase translation
steps.text: The genome is translated into a replicase polyprotein that is cleaved into the replication machinery.

steps.title: Replication organelles
steps.text: Replication and transcription take place on modified membranes and double-membrane vesicles, producing new genomes and subgenomic mRNAs.

steps.title: Assembly
steps.text: Structural proteins made from subgenomic mRNAs assemble with new genomes; particles bud into ER, intermediate-compartment or Golgi membranes.

steps.title: Release
steps.text: Virions leave the cell by exocytosis.
